subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose host IPC for Docker sandboxes, and if so should it be a narrow explicit `sandbox.docker.ipc` break-glass field rather than generic raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: The remaining request changes Docker sandbox isolation and the public config contract; current main and the latest release only prove typed GPU passthrough is already implemented.

options.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security validation or warning coverage, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Document GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and keep host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define broader namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security validation or warning coverage, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current-main policy history is the namespace-join hardening and dangerous Docker override work.
